pull_requests.title: Static Function and Resilience Gates
pull_requests.goal: Measure whether each generated structure provides usable path alternatives and barrier resilience before dynamic traffic is introduced.
scope: cross-bank connectivity under each bridge failure-group removal.
red: Create fixtures for isolated bypass, single bridge, redundant bridges, articulation chain, and true ring bypass.
Prove the metric distinguishes each pair.
green: Implement deterministic OD sampling and graph metrics.
Run all scalable styles across multiple scales and fresh seeds.
steps: Use exact topology and legal movement graph, not geometric proximity.
Define core exclusion region and gateway sets explicitly.
Keep acceptance limits predeclared or report-only if no justified bound exists.
acceptance: Isolated tangent roads fail the functional bypass test.
Each claimed redundant river case remains cross-bank connected after one failure group removal.
Every polycentric centre pair has a legal hierarchy-qualified path where claimed.
Unintended weak components are reported and block promotion.
All OD and closure selections are deterministic and serialized.

claim.allowed: specific static reachability and resilience results

stop: The benchmark starts modifying generator parameters in the same PR.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-009 as a static graph-function benchmark. Start with
adversarial fixtures that distinguish an isolated tangent road from a true
bypass and a single bridge from redundant crossings. Use legal movement
topology, deterministic OD sets, and explicit closure scenarios. Do not run
dynamic traffic or CAPR, and do not repair the generator in this PR.

pull_requests.title: Baseline Traffic-Functional Map Benchmark
pull_requests.goal: Test map function under the existing exact baseline routing and flow runtime, without CAPR or learned policies.
scope: Use one frozen routing policy and one declared traffic model per benchmark arm.
Test low, medium, and high demand plus bridge/mainline/core closures.
Measure completion/failure, p50/p95/p99 trip time, queue, spillback, no-route failures, closure recovery, conservation, and replay.
Invalidate caches correctly between topology/closure scenarios.
Compare styles at matched area, population, demand, and OD sampling.
out_of_scope: CAPR, GNN, RL, LLM, or online learning.
Generator tuning in the same PR.
red: Create minimal networks where a closure should force a legal detour.
green: Run baseline routing and declared traffic models.
Serialize full result and failure inventory.
steps: Choose point_queue_v1 as regression baseline and optionally spatial_queue_v1 as a separate declared arm.
Use identical OD/demand/event schedules across styles.
Record no-route and timeout outcomes instead of dropping them.
Do not compare means without tail and completion metrics.
Keep computational scale small enough for a personal research workflow, then add one larger diagnostic run outside required CI if needed.
acceptance: All benchmark scenarios have nonempty routable OD sets before incidents.
Every run preserves exact agent/queue mass.
Repeated runs produce identical canonical result fingerprints.
Closure scenarios either reroute through a legal alternative or produce a typed no-route outcome.
No style is declared superior from mean travel time alone.

claim.allowed: specific baseline-routing traffic results under declared synthetic scenarios
claim.not_allowed: real-world traffic validity or CAPR benefit

stop: Benchmark correctness requires changing the runtime in the same PR.
Required CI duration becomes disproportionate; move large runs to optional local evidence rather than weakening tests.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-010 as a map benchmark using existing exact baseline routing
and flow only. CAPR, neural prediction, and learning are explicitly out of
scope. Use paired OD/demand/event schedules, reject vacuous scenarios, test
cache invalidation, conservation, replay, tails, and typed no-route failures.
Keep required CI small enough for a single-developer research project; place
larger diagnostic runs outside the required gate.

pull_requests.title: Multiscale Evidence Freeze and Promotion Decision
pull_requests.goal: Combine structural, external morphology, static function, and baseline traffic evidence into one bounded APPROVE/HOLD/REJECT decision without automatically changing runtime defaults.
scope: Run the final frozen matrix at 25, 40, 100, and 250 km² where computationally feasible.
Use fresh final seeds not consumed in development or MAP-PR-008.
Aggregate G0-G5 results without allowing upper-level metrics to mask lower-level failures.
Issue per-style and overall APPROVE, HOLD, or REJECT.
Record exact commands, environment, source SHA, artifacts, and limitations.
out_of_scope: Changing generator, benchmark definitions, or thresholds.
red: Add schema tests requiring every G0-G5 stage and every style.
Add test forbidding APPROVE when a lower hard gate fails.
Add test forbidding unknown/unconsumed evidence fingerprints.
green: Assemble existing frozen evidence without recomputing or altering it.
Generate the bounded verdict and claim updates.
steps: Freeze final seed and scale matrix before execution.
Separate per-style verdicts; one failed style need not invalidate every research use.
Keep runtime default unchanged unless a later explicit user-approved PR performs that change.
Stop assurance work after the decision unless a concrete defect is observed.
acceptance: Every verdict cites exact evidence fingerprints.
No hard-gate failure is averaged away.
Unknown, missing, or stale evidence forces HOLD.
Claim ledger matches the decision package and does not duplicate volatile numeric tables.
No production source or runtime default changes.

claim.allowed: only the exact per-style decisions in the frozen package

stop: Any prerequisite artifact changes after the freeze.
A benchmark definition is changed during final evaluation.
pull_requests.codex_prompt:
Implement MAP-PR-011 only after MAP-PR-001 through MAP-PR-010 are merged.
This is a decision package, not an implementation PR. Freeze the final
multiscale/seed matrix, consume exact existing evidence fingerprints, and
issue per-style APPROVE/HOLD/REJECT decisions. A lower hard-gate failure
cannot be averaged away. Do not alter generator code, benchmark definitions,
thresholds, CAPR, or runtime defaults. After the decision, stop adding
assurance machinery unless a concrete failure requires it.
